title: CROPMED
text:
CropMED is an open dataset including areas of 191 crops (in hectares) that have been compiled and harmonized from official institutions of 48 countries in the region.




Main dataset: CropMED is primarily available as a table in comma-separated values (.csv) format, including hectares of each crop corresponding to each administrative unit and aggregated into crop groups and subgroups (see Overview).
GIS extension: CropMED is also available in GeoPackage format (.gpkg, see definition here) for intended usage in GIS programs.
Pictures: CropMED also provides multiple images showing the distribution of hectares for each crop included in the dataset. These maps can be easily visualized in the visualizer.qmd page.




Please give credit to the authors by referring to the data deposit at Zenodo as follows:   

San Segundo Molina, D., Villén Pérez, S. & Morales Castilla, I. 2026. A harmonized fine-scale crop area dataset across administrations in Europe, the Mediterranean and the Levant. Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2071710









Note



The dataset and the metadata are described from a scientific perspective in a manuscript currently under submission and review. This page will be updated to include the scientific citation as follows:
San-Segundo Molina, D., Villén-Pérez, S. & Morales-Castilla, I., 2026. CropMED: A harmonized, fine-scale crop area dataset across administrations in Europe, the Mediterranean Basin and the Levant. Journal Information To Be Completed After Publication.

title: Part I
text:
A Cancer Modeling Example
Exercise on analysis of miRNA, mRNA and protein data from the paper Aure et al, Integrated analysis reveals microRNA networks coordinately expressed with key proteins in breast cancer, Genome Medicine, 2015.
Please run the code provided to replicate some of the analyses. Make sure you can explain what all the analysis steps do and that you understand all the results.
In addition, there are some extra tasks (Task 1), where no R code is provided. Please do these tasks when you have time available at the end of the lab.

Correlation with FAO data on crop hectares for 47 countries included in CropMED



Crop hectares distribution
In the following graph, the rectangle area shows the proportion of area occupied by each crop relative to the total cropped hectares included in CropMED. 


Data validation
Overall, we found high correlation (\(R^2 = 0.094,\ \textrm{NRMSE}=0.0015\)) between data from CropMED administrative units aggregated at the country-level and those reported from FAOSTAT (https://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/QCL). Here we show the validation for some of the most relevant crops included in CropMED, where countries with higher divergences are pointed out. 


Data Quality Indicators
We assigned data quality scores to crop groups within each country across three dimensions: spatial (administrative level reached), temporal (updating periodicity of data) and taxonomic (number of unique crops reported for a crop group). The image below summarizes these scores, so that any user of the dataset can easily access the usefulness and limitations of any crop and country data.

title: About
text:
Update Plan
The CropMED dataset is intended to be updated every two years by members of the Global Change Ecology and Evolution Research group (GLOCEE) from Universidad de Alcalá. This will be done by repeating the harmonization strategy to new data as they become available in their official websites.
